subject: High tail latency from Variant B during A/B rollout — NovaRetail impact
messages:
From: Elena Park <elenap@novaretail.com>
To: support@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@novaretail.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p95/p99 spikes for /v1/generate during your A/B rollout

Hi Redwood team,

We started seeing a sharp rise in tail latency at ~08:50 PDT after you rolled the A/B experiment (Variant B) into 10% of our traffic. p95 jumped from ~420ms to ~1.1s and p99 from ~1.1s to ~3.8s. This is impacting checkout suggestions and search-autocomplete; error rates are low but throughput is suffering due to many inflight requests timing out at the client.

Can you confirm whether Variant B is known to be heavier on long prompts, or whether this is an infra anomaly? We opened an internal incident and can provide request ids and a short traffic dump if helpful (attached sample). We need an ETA for mitigation — if traffic cannot be healed quickly, please roll us back to the previous model.

Thanks,
Elena
Senior Engineering Lead, NovaRetail

Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 spikes for /v1/generate during your A/B rollout

Quick triage notes (initial):
- We see elevated token decode time and KV cache miss amplification on Variant B for long prompts (>800 tokens). p95 from our metrics portal aligns with NovaRetail’s reported numbers: 420ms -> ~1.1s, p99 -> ~3.5s - 4.0s.
- Variant B uses a different attention kernel and a slightly different kv-cache layout (quantization + fused-kernel path). On this workload it appears to lose the favorable cache locality that Variant A had.
- No cluster-wide IO saturation and no throttling at the network layer; issue is variant-specific and reproducible on a small sample.

Immediate remediation actions I recommend now:
1) Abort the A/B rollout and reassign NovaRetail traffic back to Variant A immediately (we can route at the load-balancer with a single config flip).
2) If rollback requires 2FA window, trigger emergency rollback policy to bypass it for this customer’s traffic.
3) Collect side-by-side traces for 1 hour with X-Request-Ids to drive a deeper fix; attach p99 CSV.

I can execute 1) now if Rafael/Ben give the green light; it should take <4 minutes to complete and we’ll monitor p95/p99 to validate.

-Markus
Sr. Performance Engineer, Serving Runtime

Hi Elena — we’ve confirmed the canary variant (Variant B) is the likely cause after an initial engineering check. We are initiating an immediate rollback of your traffic to the previously stable Variant A and will monitor.

What we’re doing now (ETA and actions):
- Traffic will be reassigned to Variant A within the next ~5 minutes (action: rollback initiated)
- We’ll monitor p95/p99 for the next 30 minutes and share metrics and traces (action: monitoring + artifacts)
- Markus will pull side-by-side traces to identify the kernel/cache mismatch and propose a patch; we’ll follow up with a timeline for a safe re-release after validation (action: root cause analysis)

I’ll confirm once latency is back to baseline. We’ll also open an incident (INC-4123) and send a concise executive update for your CTO. Sorry for the disruption and thanks for the quick signal.

Best,
Rafael

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 16:43:00 -0700
Subject: NovaRetail rollback completed — exec brief and next steps

FYI exec note:
- Incident: Variant B caused p95/p99 regression for NovaRetail during a targeted A/B rollout at 08:50 PDT; customer impact: degraded autocomplete and search latency, increased client-side timeouts for some requests.
- Action taken: Immediate rollback of NovaRetail traffic to Variant A completed at 10:17 PDT. Post-rollback monitoring shows p95 back to ~410-430ms and p99 trending to ~1.0s within 25 minutes.
- Cause (preliminary): Variant B’s attention kernel path amplifies KV cache misses on long prompts. Not an infra network failure.
- Customer comms: Rafael sent an apology and committed to a timeline for a safe re-release after mitigations. Ben is handling CTO-level touch and potential renewal sensitivity.
- Next steps: engineering to: (a) reproduce at scale in staging with long prompt workload, (b) attempt kernel fallback with identical kv layout, (c) add new perf regression test to our canary gating for long prompt tails.

I’m available to brief the leadership team if you want a short 15-minute sync.

-Marissa
Director, Customer Success
